title: Logistics Intelligence Planner (MSgt to Cpl) NMOS (0211, 0231, 0241, 0261), DIR INTEL
raw_text:
6. MOS 0234, Logistics Intelligence Planner (MSgt to Cpl) NMOS (0211, 0231,
0241, 0261), DIR INTEL

    a. Summary. Logistics Intelligence Planners are subject matter experts
in providing intelligence support to logistics planning, conducting
intelligence support to Physical Network Analysis (PNA), and integrating
intelligence into the six functions of tactical logistics. Logistics
Intelligence Planners forecast intelligence requirements unique to the LCE
and are experts at integrating those requirements into the MAGTF or Fleet
intelligence collection and production plans.

    b. Prerequisites.       Security requirement:   SCI security clearance
eligibility.

    c. Requirements. Must successfully complete the Logistics Intelligence
Planners Course (LIPC) (M090JQ9) at MCLOG.

    d. Duties. For a complete list of duties, refer to reference (g),
Intelligence Training and Readiness Manual.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.
common_text: The Intelligence OccFld conducts the collection, processing, and dissemination of intelligence. The specialties within the Intelligence OccFld are analysis, counterintelligence, imagery intelligence, geospatial intelligence and human intelligence. Basic qualification requirements include clerical, communication, and computer skills. Intelligence Specialists are required to learn and master a variety of analytical and technical skills. Formal schooling is mandatory for assignment of an intelligence MOS. Entry-level Marines enter the field in MOS 0231, Intelligence Specialist, MOS 0241, Imagery Analyst, or MOS 0261, Geospatial Intelligence Specialist. Entry into MOS 0211, Counterintelligence/Human Intelligence (CI/HUMINT) Specialist is accomplished by lateral move. Duty assignments vary widely from all levels of the operating forces to joint staffs, to unified commands. Intelligence Marines have the opportunity to serve in billets such as drill instructor, recruiter, and Marine security guard duty. Marines entering the OccFld will receive MOS 0200, Basic Intelligence Marine, while participating in on-the job training (if required) and/or attending formal school. All Marines assigned an intelligence MOS must submit a single scope background investigation (SSBI) prior to attending formal school. Intelligence MOS Marines must have an adjudicated SSBI to qualify for assignment of one of the primary intelligence MOSs. Intelligence MOS Marines are required to have a defense language aptitude battery (DLAB) test score on file in their official military personnel file (OMPF). There is no minimum DLAB score required before being assigned as 02XX PMOS. Intelligence MOSs are assigned and voided only by the Commandant of the Marine Corps (MM) in coordination with the OccFld specialist’s recommendations.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
